title: Integer-valued polynomials over a one-dimensional analytically irreducible local domain form a free module: Elliott's non-flatness conjectures fail
subject: math.AC
abstract: In 2011 J. Elliott conjectured that the ring $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ of integer-valued polynomials is not flat over $D=\mathbf F_2[[T^2,T^3]]$, nor over $D=\mathbf F_2+T\mathbf F_4[[T]]$, and more generally that some local, Noetherian, one-dimensional, analytically irreducible domain has a non-flat $\operatorname{Int}(D)$. This spring H. Ma, with the reasoning system Rethlas, answered Problem 19 of Cahen, Fontana, Frisch and Glaz negatively, with a local domain whose normalization has two maximal ideals. We prove that Elliott's conjectures fail. For the first of his rings, Elliott himself announced freeness in 2013, without a published proof that we could find. If $D$ is a subring of a discrete valuation ring $V$ with finite residue field, and $D$ contains a nonzero ideal of $V$, then $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ is a free $D$-module. Consequently $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ is free for every one-dimensional analytically irreducible Noetherian local domain $D$. By Elliott's own theorems, the canonical maps $\operatorname{Int}(D)^{\otimes n}\to\operatorname{Int}(D^n)$ are then isomorphisms and $\operatorname{Int}(D)$ carries a unique compatible biring structure. For Elliott's two rings we write down the polynomials explicitly. The proof patches two free modules along the conductor square and uses a matrix identity of Whitehead and a theorem of Kaplansky. The proof was produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode). The corollary for analytically irreducible domains and the explicit examples were written by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, which also checked the proof; Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked the whole note again. No human has checked this note.
comments:
Version 2 credits J. Elliott's announcement (an addition of 26 December 2013 to his MathOverflow question 75202) that Int(F_2[[T^2,T^3]]) is free, which version 1 omitted, and adds that reference; the mathematics is unchanged. This note refutes Conjectures 2.10, 2.15 and 2.17 of J. Elliott (Integer-valued polynomial rings, t-closure, and associated primes, Comm. Algebra 39 (2011)) and answers Problems 19-21 of Cahen, Fontana, Frisch and Glaz positively for one-dimensional analytically irreducible local domains. It complements H. Ma's negative answer to Problem 19 (arXiv:2604.05922) and the answer to Problem 21 of Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu (arXiv:2605.25259), whose domain has two branches; neither result implies the other. The tools are Bhargava's regular bases, Milnor's patching, a matrix identity of Whitehead and Kaplansky's theorem.

Checks: the proof was checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, which wrote the text, the corollary and the examples (verified by exact series arithmetic), and again in full by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max. No human has checked it. Records, checks and the program: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches/blob/main/works/WB-0004.md
provenance:
Text: AI-authored; none of it was written by a human. The submitter takes responsibility for the veracity of the text.

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, proved Theorem 1 in November 2026, in a research run on the operations on integer-valued polynomials that arise from the Montpellier manuscripts of A. Grothendieck, prompted by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) at effort max. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, wrote the present text on 23 November 2026 from the run's proof, read the literature at the locators given, and wrote the reduction of Corollary 2, the reading of Corollary 3 through Elliott's theorems, and the two explicit examples.

How it was checked. All checks are of 23 November 2026. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, checked every step of the proof; the examples were verified by an exact program (400 random arguments, series to precision t^56 and t^52). Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, read the whole note and followed every step, read Stacks Project Tag 032Y at the source and recomputed both examples by hand. Corollary 3 rests on Elliott's theorems of 2007 and 2010 as Cahen, Fontana, Frisch and Glaz and Elliott (2011) recall them; those papers were not opened. A search of Hexagon on 23 November 2026 found nothing on Int(D) as a module. No human has checked the proof or the text, and nothing is formalized.

Where the records are. https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches/blob/main/works/WB-0004.md
